title: Network formation and dynamics among multi-LLMs
rationale: Strongest L4 hit. Multiple LLM agents form network links; prompts expose node degrees, neighbors, common connections, community labels, and in some settings full network/neighborhood structure. This is agent-facing global abstract network structure rather than only researcher-side analysis.

title: Leveraging LLM-based agents for social science research: insights from citation network simulations
rationale: CiteAgent simulates citation-network evolution and exposes citation-related attributes such as paper citation and author citation. It may qualify as L4 if the review accepts science-of-science citation networks as a digital social environment, but it is farther from spatial-social systems than L4R-01.

title: LLM Agents for Smart City Management: Enhancing Decision Support Through Multi-Agent AI Systems
rationale: The system exposes accessibility, connectivity, centrality, service coverage, and geospatial layers through a Digital Urban Platform API. However it is a smart-city decision-support architecture, not a social simulation or socially situated interaction system.

title: Cognitive Agents in Urban Mobility: Integrating LLM Reasoning into Multi-Agent Simulations
rationale: Already included as R3-03 bridge_core. The environment is geospatial/transport-network based, but available evidence supports L3 route/location/context exposure rather than global abstract configurational indicators in the agent input.

title: S3: Social-network Simulation System with Large Language Model-Empowered Agents
rationale: Already included as BK07 bridge_core. Recheck found follow graph, followee message exposure, profiles, memory, and propagation, but no agent-facing centrality/community/global topology summary.

title: Unveiling the collective behaviors of large language model-based autonomous agents in an online community: A social network analysis perspective
rationale: Already included as BK08 bridge_core. Centralization, homophily, power-law, and small-world comparisons are researcher-side SNA outputs rather than agent-facing global structure.
